answer.line: E2: one step, no cation, nothing shifts. The only beta H are on the methyl, so the C=C forms at the chain end.

steps: List the beta carbons, the neighbors of the C-Br carbon: the CH3 at C1 and the quaternary C3, which has no H.
E2 pulls a beta H as Br leaves, in a single step. No cation ever forms, so no methyl can shift.
Only C1 has hydrogens, so only one alkene is possible: 3,3-dimethylbut-1-ene. Zaitsev has nothing to choose between.

choices.note: This skeleton needs a methyl shift, and a shift needs a carbocation, as in E1 with no strong base. E2 never makes one.
The only beta H is on the methyl, so the C=C forms at the end.
The most substituted alkene pulls you because of Zaitsev. Reaching it takes a methyl shift through a cation, which is the E1 product when no strong base is present.
Ethoxide can substitute, but this carbon is secondary and sits next to a tert-butyl group. Crowding plus heat hands it to E2.
An alcohol needs water or hydroxide as the nucleophile. This flask holds ethoxide in ethanol.

lockIt: E2 is concerted: no cation, no shift, and it needs a beta H.
